advertisements.title: Learning never ends!❤️
advertisements.description:
Learning never ends!❤️

Our Vendors learns the 7Ms of Filipino Core Values.

1. Maka-Diyos (God-centered) – Acts with integrity and respect.
2. Makatao (People-oriented) – Shows empathy, kindness, and compassion.
3. Makakalikasan (Environmentally conscious) – Cares for and protects the environment.
4. Makabansa (Patriotic) – Takes pride in and promotes the Philippines.
5. Masayahin (Cheerful) – Greets others with warmth, positivity, and a smile.
6. May Bayanihan (Community-driven) – Works together and helps others willingly.
7. May Pag-asa (Hopeful) – Maintains optimism and resilience. 

#DASIGTITAY

newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay MFS Shift B duty personnel received a report from a concerned citizen requesting emergency medical assistance in Achasol, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay Province. Titay MFS Shift B personnel immediately responded to the scene.
Upon arrival at the scene, the patient was found seated on a chair, conscious and alert. The patient presented with elevated blood pressure of 160/90 mmHg and complained of right-sided body weakness, slurred speech, and dizziness. The patient reported a history of hypertension and had been taking Amlodipine 5 mg as maintenance medication since last year.
An initial assessment was immediately conducted. Due to the patient's presenting signs and symptoms, the patient was carefully assisted and transferred to the ambulance using a two-man carry technique for further assessment, monitoring, and transport to an appropriate medical facility.
The patient was immediately transported to Dr. George T Hofer Medical Center for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at Dr. George T Hofer Medical Center, Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, the patient was properly endorsed to the attending medical staff on duty.

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay MFS Shift B duty personnel received a report of a medical emergency in Kitabog, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. The responding personnel were immediately dispatched and promptly proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary medical assistance.
Upon arrival at the scene, the patient was found conscious, alert, and oriented while being carried by his mother. The patient had been experiencing diarrhea for four (4) days. Earlier today, the patient had been discharged after a three-day admission at Dr. Perlie B. Sibud County Hospital. However, following his discharge at approximately 1500H, the patient continued to experience diarrhea, with more than five (5) episodes reported.
An initial assessment was conducted to determine the patient's current condition and need for immediate medical intervention and transport. The patient was carried to the ambulance by EMS personnel.
The patient was immediately transported to Dr. Henry R. De Villa Memorial Hospital, Poblacion, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for further medical evaluation and management.
Upon arrival at Dr. Henry R. De Villa Memorial Hospital, Poblacion, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, the patient was properly endorsed to the medical staff on duty.

newsArticles.summary:

𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station (MFS) Shift A duty personnel responded to a medical emergency in Barangay Azusano, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. Upon receipt of the report, Shift A duty personnel were immediately dispatched and proceeded to the scene to provide the necessary emergency medical assistance.  Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team found a female patient lying supine on a bed and unresponsive. 

A primary assessment was immediately conducted to evaluate her airway, breathing, circulation, level of consciousness, and overall condition.  Immediate life-saving measures were initiated by maintaining a patent airway and performing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) at a ratio of 30 chest compressions to 2 ventilations per cycle. 

The patient's condition and response to resuscitation efforts were continuously monitored throughout the intervention.  The patient was immediately transported via BFP ambulance to Dr. George T. Hofer Medical Center, Barangay Tenan, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay, for further medical evaluation, treatment, and management. Resuscitative measures and continuous monitoring were maintained as appropriate during transport. 

𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.

newsArticles.summary:
𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘 𝐌𝐄𝐃𝐈𝐂𝐀𝐋 𝐑𝐄𝐒𝐏𝐎𝐍𝐒𝐄 
𝐈𝐍 𝐏𝐇𝐎𝐓𝐎𝐒 || Titay Municipal Fire Station Shift A duty personnel received a report from a concerned citizen requesting an emergency medical response in Poblacion, Titay, Zamboanga Sibugay. In response, Titay MFS Shift A personnel immediately proceeded to the reported location to render appropriate emergency medical assistance.  Upon arrival at the scene, the responding team conducted a primary assessment, including an evaluation of the patient's level of consciousness, presence of bleeding, and possible injuries. The patient was found conscious, alert, and oriented, and was seated in the corner of the classroom. Assessment revealed a suspected fracture of the left knee.  Immediate first aid was rendered by applying a splint to the suspected fracture to immobilize the affected left knee and help prevent further injury during transport.  The patient was immediately transported to De Villa Hospital for further medical evaluation and management.    
 𝐈𝐍 𝐂𝐀𝐒𝐄 𝐎𝐅 𝐄𝐌𝐄𝐑𝐆𝐄𝐍𝐂𝐘, call 911 or contact the Titay MFS Hotline Number: 0965-509-0944.
#SaBFPLigtasAngMayAlam
#TitayMFS
#EmergencyMedicalResponse

newsArticles.title: FO1 Carido Brings World-Class Emergency Care Home
newsArticles.summary:
FO1 Carido Brings World-Class Emergency Care Home
Titay Municipal Fire Station celebrates another milestone as FO1 Arven T Carido successfully completed the prestigious Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) and Tactical Emergency Casualty Care (TECC) Training Program in Taiwan from June 22–30, 2026.
FO1 Carido was among only 54 BFP emergency responders nationwide selected for the international training. The program equipped participants with advanced skills in tactical emergency medicine, pre-hospital care, disaster response, and high-risk rescue operations.
His achievement is a source of pride for Titay MFS, as the knowledge and expertise he gained will further strengthen the station's emergency medical response capabilities, ensuring faster, safer, and more effective life-saving services for the people of Titay. Through this international learning experience, Titay MFS continues its commitment to delivering emergency response that meets global standards while serving the local community with excellence.
